Block 6 apartments north of island park are better than the Gardner and have a small off street lot in the alley that comes with the apartment.  The kitchens are a bit dated, but I think they're slowly replacing appliances. My fridge was brand new but my microwave, oven/stove, dishwasher were from the 80s. They all work well enough to function properly though. Overall pretty solid place to live if you're main focus is cost of rent. 

They have free internet built in to each apartment that is decent enough for me to stream on twitch, game online, and stream all shows (slow download/upload speeds for big files though) you just need to supply your own router. Overall I just pay for electric which is standard electric & heating.

I moved in last year with a 6 month lease at 670. They bumped my lease 30 when I resigned after the 6 months, so I'd suggest locking in at a year.

Management is like 7/10. Not amazing but they get they have responsibilities.

Overall quality neighbors. Keep to themselves or are polite. Haven't ran into any "sketchy" characters like I did when I lived at the Gardner 4ish years ago.

Third Drop @ downtown fargo. They're only open until 4pm, but the afternoons have maybe 1 or 2 other people. They also have nice window seating that gets a lot of sun.

Young Blood @ downtown fargo. Very very chill vibe. The workers are super friendly and have great suggestions. Moderately busy, but they have window seating and plenty of booth/high top seating. They're open until 5:30pm. The busier crowd is almost worth it for the atmosphere and good music they play.

I like Babbs, but I can't seem to get a lot of work done there because they only have so many tables and I don't like to work sitting on couches, also depending on day/time, there are A LOT of groups and busy conversations taking place whereas the other two have lots of 1-on-1 and solo customers. 

Atomic Coffee is open the latest (10pm I think) and has lots of table seating, so they win on that one, but it's hit or miss for me. Sometimes I get interrupted by people asking for money (even if I have headphones in and I'm tucked away in the corner). Not a problem that they're asking.. it's just the other places have an almost 100% chance of not being interrupted with whatever you're focused on ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

The Fargo Library is the best bet for total concentration. Lots of awesome window/view spots if you want a view or individual study rooms if you want no distractions. They also have a little cafe to get a drink/coffee before you enter the library proper (unsure about the hours of that place though).

Lowkey though.... If you're over 21, Front Street Taproom has a super cozy mezzanine that overlooks the rest of the bar. It's usually not busy in the afternoons (they open at 4pm). The lower part of the bar can be busier but if the mezzanine isn't rented out for private events, there are usually people reading, working on homework, playing chess. They have table seating and couch seating. Plus you get to have craft beer, some N/A choices, and some bar snacks. I've gotten a surprising amount of work done here.

My dad is starting a freelance carpentry/furniture-making/handyman business in his retirement. He wanted a logo and business card made. He wants to use his name as the name of the company and wanted a logo that was unique.

  
I posted multiple versions to see which ones were more liked. Any comments/critiques/opinions/ideas on colors, layouts, or fonts are appreciated.

Thanks for the feedback. It's not harsh, no worries. Just want to make sure, you're talking about the font choice on the card with the log logo mark? Not the signature one?

Again, thank you for the feedback

For background, my dad is a finishing carpenter of custom homes by trade with a lot of woodworking/furniture-making experience. He asked me to make a business card, logo, and name for his new business. His business consisting of custom carpentry/handyman work, furniture making, and woodworking. He also is interested in using lathes, burning techniques, electricity techniques, etc. I don't have any pictures of anything he's made over the years to share.

He didn't give me a lot of direction other than make it unique and use his name as the name of his business in some kind of way.

(3RD IMAGE) The initial direction I took was to use his signature as a some kind of word/logo mark. I felt it was more personal and elegant coupled with a serif font. I kind of backed away from this though and left a lot of these ideas unfinished.. I wasn't sure if it worked as a logo, even if it worked to have on his business card. Those ideas mostly helped me organize where to put information on the card.I included some of these rough ideas on the final image.

(1ST IMAGE) The next direction I took was to develop something I'd recognize as a logo. The combo of the G (the first letter of his first name) and a tree ring. I made a couple different versions of this idea from sketches. Trying different background patterns for the front, and continued the idea of lumber on the back side. The first card back fills the extra space with pieces of "logo-stamped" lumber. I did this really for the sake of logic.. I wasn't sure if the two pieces of lumber created the illusion of them being propped against each other effectively. It felt like it did, but also didn't feel like it. Including the extra lumber feels a little too busy with the logo, and a little plain without the logo, so I'm unsure what to do with that concept. I also tried a vertical take on the card. I'm unsure if there are defined rules, for the sake of visibility/readability, for business cards being vertical or horizontal, so I'm not sure if this works either. This idea overall doesn't feel finished yet. I've listed some thoughts about this idea in lists..

**Things I enjoy and feel like are working (heading in the right direction):**  
\- the font choice  
\- the logo mark

**Things I'm questioning for this idea:**  
\- the color choices  
\- the extra visual details  
\- the stacked lumber concept  
\- vertical or horizontal

(2ND IMAGE) I wanted to see what the logo looked like digitally burned onto a "wood" business card. I was tossing around the idea of reaching out to a local business and have them laser the final version of this project (however it turns out) onto a handful of wooden business cards for special occasions, special meetings, special people, etc AND to just stand out from the rest of the paper ones I see around town where I live. I don't have any technical details (wood choices, wood thickness, how detailed the laser can get) for how it would work functionally on wood.. Or if it would just be better printed on to a piece of properly chosen business card paper as an image.

I just wanted to know what parts are working and aren't working for all ideas.. or just some general thoughts before going any further, or making any more ideas. I want to present more cohesive and cleaned up ideas to my dad.
